The rodent has a specialized diet and unusually small litter size for a rodent, suggesting a life-history strategy favoring fewer offspring with more care per offspring.  
High parental investment often correlates with small litter sizes to increase survival of each offspring.  
Precocial young (C) is unlikely because rodents generally have altricial young.  
Sexual dimorphism (A) and extrapair matings (D) are more common in species with higher reproductive rates and less parental care.  

Final answer: (B)
